stories.headline: Iran prepares terms to reopen Strait of Hormuz during US conflict
stories.body:
Iranian official Mohsen Rezaei announced that Iran is drawing up conditions to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Mediators asked Tehran to set out its terms. Rezaei serves as secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council. He said Iran exported 80 million barrels of oil during a ceasefire period.

Under a June memorandum of understanding, Iran agreed to clear mines. Iran also agreed to permit free vessel passage in the Strait of Hormuz for 60 days. In return, the United States agreed to lift its blockade. The US also agreed to ease sanctions.

US President Donald Trump rejected re-establishing the terms of that June agreement. Oil prices rose after reports of his decision. Trump declared in the Oval Office that US forces had cleared mines from the Strait of Hormuz. He said that the waterway was open. Trump later told Al Jazeera that he has no time schedule for negotiations with Iran. He said he is in no hurry to resume talks.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced sanctions named Operation Economic Outcast. The sanctions target nearly 60 Iran-linked individuals, entities, and vessels. The measures aim to pressure Iran during the war with the US. Rezaei warned that Iran will target US economic interests 100 percent if the US blockade continues. He said Iran will act with intensity and force.

Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said Iran has the legitimate right to target the origin of any act of aggression. He pointed specifically to US refueling aircraft departing from Bulgaria. Qatari Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in Tehran. They met to discuss regional security and conditions for dialogue.

The conflict has affected military readiness elsewhere. US defense and NATO officials said the US military faces a critical shortage of Patriot missile interceptors in Europe. The shortage happened because interceptor stocks were redeployed to the Middle East for the war with Iran. The Wall Street Journal reported that CIA Director John Ratcliffe traveled to Moscow. He went to warn Russia not to attack NATO countries.

In Australia, environmental authorities face avian health issues. A common dolphin found near Goolwa in South Australia tested positive for H5 bird flu. It is the second native mammal species in Australia confirmed with the virus. The Australian government decided to withdraw 24 expeditioners from its Macquarie Island research station. The government took action because of psychosocial risks from an expected H5 avian influenza mortality event.

Qatari Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in Tehran to discuss regional security and conditions for dialogue.

US defence and NATO officials stated that the US military faces a critical shortage of Patriot missile interceptors in Europe due to interceptor stocks being redeployed to the Middle East for the war with Iran.

stories.headline: Trump orders federal agencies to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America
stories.body:
US President Donald Trump signed an executive order directing the Department of the Interior to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America. Lake Ontario lies along the border separating New York from the Canadian province of Ontario. The name originates from the Huron Indigenous word oniatari:io, meaning lake of shining waters.

The US Geological Survey updated the name in its Geographic Names Information System. Democratic Representative Debbie Dingell of Michigan announced plans to introduce legislation in Congress to nullify the order.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said on social media that Canadians know things must be called by their name. Carney said the lake is called Lake Ontario today and forever.

Trump previously issued an executive order renaming the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America. That order led to a legal dispute with Mexico and a lawsuit by the Associated Press. Trump also posted an altered 1948 Life magazine graphic on social media. The graphic placed him at the top under a new category named greatest.

Trade tensions between the countries remain high. The US put 50% tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian goods. The tariffs were imposed after trade negotiations collapsed between Washington and Ottawa. Canadian trade minister Dominic LeBlanc said on X that the US withdrew demands on French language labeling.

The name Lake Ontario originates from the Huron Indigenous word oniatari:io, meaning lake of shining waters.
The US Geological Survey updated the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America in its Geographic Names Information System following President Trump's order.

stories.headline: Meta agrees to multi-billion settlements over youth safety claims
stories.body:
Tech company Meta agreed to pay major financial settlements to resolve state and federal child safety lawsuits in the United States. One report stated Meta agreed to pay $18 billion to settle a lawsuit from 29 US states. Another report put the 29-state settlement figure at $16.68 billion.

Meta also reached a broader deal covering 47 states and territories for up to $17.1 billion in penalties. That deal includes a separate $1 billion settlement in Texas. Meta agreed to pay up to $17 billion to settle a federal lawsuit brought by California, Colorado, Kentucky, and New Jersey. Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers approved the multi-state agreement in federal court in Oakland, California.

As part of the settlement, Meta agreed to implement a default two-hour daily time limit for users under 18. Meta will also set a default block on nighttime use. It will ban displaying like and reaction counts.

British minister Pat McFadden said the UK does not want American children receiving higher protection than British children.

In 2025, Meta generated $198.8 billion in revenue and $102.5 billion in operating profit.

claims.text: Meta settled a lawsuit brought by 29 US states accusing it of designing addictive products for young people, agreeing to pay $18 billion and alter platform features in the US.
Meta agreed to pay up to $17 billion in penalties to settle a landmark federal child safety lawsuit brought by California, Colorado, Kentucky, and New Jersey.
Meta agreed to pay $16.68 billion to settle claims from 29 US states alleging it designed its apps to addict teenagers and improperly harvested children's data.
Meta reached a settlement agreement covering 47 states and several territories for up to $17.1 billion in penalties, alongside a separate $1 billion settlement in Texas.
Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers approved Meta's multi-state settlement agreement in federal court in Oakland, California.

As part of its proposed settlement, Meta agreed to implement a default two-hour daily time limit for users under 18, a default block on nighttime use, and a ban on displaying like and reaction counts.
British minister Pat McFadden stated that the UK government does not want a situation where children in the US receive a higher level of protection than children in the UK.
In 2025, Meta's family of apps segment generated $198.8 billion in revenue and $102.5 billion in operating profit.

stories.headline: Glacial collapse triggers fatal flood in Nepal and Tibet region
stories.body:
A massive glacial collapse triggered sudden flash floods along the Nepal-Tibet border, killing hundreds of people and leaving many missing. The US Geological Survey clarified that a collapsed glacier caused the disaster. The impact of the falling glacier hitting the valley floor registered a seismic magnitude of 5.2.

An analysis by ICIMOD found that an ice-rock avalanche entered the Lende Khola tributary. The flood caused downstream river levels to rise by 7 to 9 metres within 30 minutes. The disaster occurred in Nepal's northern Rasuwa district without earlier rainfall in the immediate area to warn residents. Flooding struck along the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river systems.

Nepal Police reported that 469 people died as of Friday. Police reported that 1,545 people were rescued or injured. Authorities deployed 4,348 police personnel for search and rescue operations across affected districts. Nepali army helicopter rescue teams worked to rescue about 100 people trapped inside a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A hydropower project.

Hundreds of foreign citizens remain missing in Nepal. Nepal Police reported that missing foreigners include 178 Indians, 65 Americans, 51 Malaysians, 53 Ukrainians, 33 Britons, 35 Australians, and 25 Canadians. India's Ministry of External Affairs said that 290 Indians in Nepal remain unaccounted for. The ministry added that about 200 Indians stranded on the Chinese side after the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra sought assistance.

Across the border in Tibet, Chinese state media reported that at least 558 people were missing. That number includes at least 260 foreign nationals. Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported that 555 stranded tourists and 499 local residents were transported out of the disaster zone in Tibet by Friday morning.

Individual families are searching for news of loved ones. Rakesh Nayak, a 45-year-old software engineer from Karnataka living in Australia, went missing near the border during an Isha Foundation tour. He was last known to be inside an immigration office at about 9:10 pm on August 26. Flash floods struck twenty minutes later. At least 13 people from Karnataka are stranded in Nepal and Tibet.

Nepal declined search and rescue team deployment offers from foreign countries. Offers came from India, China, the US, UK, Japan, South Korea, Sri Lanka, and Bangladesh. The United States pledged $500,000, and the World Health Organization sent emergency medical supplies. UN humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher released $2 million in emergency funds. The Red Cross launched an emergency appeal for $31 million to help an estimated 93,000 affected people.

stories.headline: Indian tribunal approves 99.97% debt haircut for Subhash Chandra
stories.body:
The National Company Law Tribunal approved a personal insolvency plan for Essel Group chairman Subhash Chandra. The ruling allows Chandra to pay Rs 6.5 crore against creditor claims of over Rs 22,000 crore. Under the plan, creditors will recover about 0.028% of their claims, or three paise for every Rs 100 owed. For example, LIC Housing Finance had an admitted claim of Rs 1,322.39 crore, but its approved repayment is Rs 38,09,294.

NCLT Member Nilesh Sharma approved the plan as a third member after a split verdict by a two-member bench. Creditors holding 80.8% of voting rights approved the plan. Dissenting lenders representing about 15% argued that related entities like Veena Investments controlled over 61% of votes. HDFC Bank said it is exploring an appeal against the 99.97% debt haircut.

Political opposition leaders criticized the ruling. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi called the tribunal the Neta-Company Loot Tribunal. Congress leader Jairam Ramesh called the 99.97% debt reduction a mockery of insolvency laws. Chandra's office said he was only a personal guarantor and had not borrowed money personally. Chandra served as an Independent MP backed by the BJP from 2016 to 2022.

claims.text: The National Company Law Tribunal approved a personal insolvency repayment plan allowing Essel Group chairman Subhash Chandra to pay Rs 6.5 crore against creditor claims of over Rs 22,000 crore.
Under the approved plan, creditors are expected to recover approximately 0.028% of their original admitted claims, or about three paise for every Rs 100 owed.
For LIC Housing Finance's admitted claim of Rs 1,322.39 crore, the approved repayment amount was Rs 38,09,294.

NCLT Member (Judicial) Nilesh Sharma approved Subhash Chandra's resolution plan under Section 114 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code as the third member following a split verdict by a two-member bench.
Creditors representing 80.8% of voting rights approved Subhash Chandra's repayment plan, while dissenting creditors represented around 15%.
Dissenting lenders argued that assenting creditors such as Veena Investments were related entities controlling over 61% of voting rights and were ineligible under Section 109(4)(b) of the IBC.
HDFC Bank stated it is exploring an appeal against the NCLT order granting a 99.97% haircut on personal guarantee claims against Subhash Chandra.
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi criticized the ruling on X, referring to the NCLT as the 'Neta-Company Loot Tribunal'.
Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh described the 99.97% debt reduction approved by NCLT as a 'mundan' that makes a mockery of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code.
Subhash Chandra's office stated that he was only a personal guarantor for corporate loans and had not borrowed money personally from creditors.
Subhash Chandra served as an Independent Rajya Sabha MP backed by the Bharatiya Janata Party from 2016 to 2022.

vocab.meaning: the state of being unable to pay debts owed
a person who promises to pay a debt if the borrower fails to pay

stories.headline: Narendra Modi plans visit to Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan for summit
stories.body:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi will begin a four-day visit to Uzbekistan and the Kyrgyz Republic on August 29. Modi will visit Uzbekistan from August 29 to 30 before traveling to the Kyrgyz Republic from August 31 to September 1.

In Tashkent, Modi will hold talks with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev to strengthen their strategic partnership. Bilateral trade and investment between India and Uzbekistan stand close to $1 billion. More than 16,000 Indian students study in Uzbekistan, which hosts four Indian university campuses. Modi will also visit the Lal Bahadur Shastri Memorial and the Mahatma Gandhi Centre.

Modi will then attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek. The summit marks the 25th anniversary of the organization, which India joined in 2017. On the sidelines, Modi will hold a bilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Ahead of the summit, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar met Putin in Moscow. Putin assured Jaishankar that Russia will continue supplying fertilizers to Indian farmers.

Modi is also scheduled to host Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in India for a BRICS summit on September 12 and 13.

PM Modi is scheduled to host Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in India for the BRICS summit on September 12-13.
